questions.question: At the top price, Mahanadi Coalfields Ltd.'s P/E is 8.43x. Similar listed companies have a P/E of about 9.94x. What does that tell you?

choices.text: It costs about the same as, or less than, similar companies for each rupee of profit.
It costs more than similar companies for each rupee of profit, so its profit must grow faster to be worth it.
The P/E shows how many shares the company has.

questions.explanation: A P/E of 8.43x against 9.94x means you pay no more for each rupee of Mahanadi Coalfields Ltd.'s profit than for its peers'. That is a fair starting point, not a guarantee.

questions.question: 134.2% of this IPO's money is an offer for sale. Where does that part of the money go?

choices.text: Into the company, to build new factories.
To the existing owners who are selling their shares.

questions.explanation: In an offer for sale, existing owners sell shares they already hold, so the money goes to them. Only the fresh issue, ₹-2,295.24 crore here, reaches Mahanadi Coalfields Ltd..

questions.question: Sales went from ₹31,634.35 crore in FY24 to ₹30,549.59 crore in FY26, which is -1.7% a year. How would you describe that?
questions.explanation: -1.7% a year is barely growing, or shrinking: Mahanadi Coalfields Ltd. isn't selling much more than before.

questions.question: Mahanadi Coalfields Ltd. owes 0 rupees of loans for every rupee of its owners' money. Which is closest to the truth?

choices.text: Its loans are small to manageable next to what the owners have put in.
Its loans are heavy: lenders have more riding on it than its owners.
Loans never matter for a company that makes a profit.

questions.explanation: At 0 rupees of loans per rupee of owners' money, Mahanadi Coalfields Ltd.'s owners have more in the business than its lenders.
